instructions: Put the pine nuts in a dry large skillet over medium heat. Toast them for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking the pan, until they're golden and smell nutty. Transfer them to a plate.
In a large bowl, mix 2 tsp salt, the coriander, paprika, nutmeg, black pepper and cloves. Stir in the vinegar.
Add the lamb and mix it with your hands for about 2 minutes, until the meat looks sticky and holds together.
Divide the meat into 16 pieces and roll each into a short log about 2 1/2 inches long. Wet your hands if the meat sticks.
Heat the olive oil in the same skillet over medium heat. Lay the makanek in a single layer with a little space between them.
Cook for 7 minutes, turning every 1 to 2 minutes, until they're browned on all sides.
Add 1/4 cup of water to the pan and cover it right away. Stand back a little, it will spit. Cook for 3 minutes.

Uncover and cook for 2 minutes, until the water has cooked off. You're cooking them to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Turn the heat down to medium-low. Add the pomegranate molasses and the juice of the lemon (about 3 tbsp), and toss for about 1 minute, until the glaze thickens and coats the makanek.
Taste one. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Chop 1/4 cup of parsley. Top the makanek with the toasted pine nuts and the parsley, and serve.
method_notes: No source has a 30 minute version, so this takes Hadia's Lebanese Cuisine for the spicing (coriander, paprika, nutmeg, black and white pepper, cloves, a splash of red vinegar) and the finish of lemon juice and pomegranate molasses. It skips the sheep casings and the 24 hour chill of Hadia's casing-free version: the meat is rolled into short logs and browned, then steamed briefly with a splash of water as Zaffaron does, which lets it cook through in minutes. Sofra Beirut also finishes ready-made links with pomegranate molasses, lemon and parsley. Pine nuts are toasted as a garnish instead of being mixed into the meat. The white pepper is left out and the garlic and allspice of Zaffaron's version are not used.
